# Odds snapshots, results and forecasts

This branch holds data, not code. The `Odds snapshot` workflow on the `main` branch adds a commit here for each snapshot it takes, normally six a day. Each commit records, for every upcoming NBA game, the home team's chance of winning as US sportsbooks price it. Once a day, with the first snapshot of the day, it also records how the games that are over ended and whether the side that the sportsbooks favored won. The same daily run rebuilds two models from the results of the season, Elo and a points-and-rest model, writes their forecasts for the games of the day to a file that is never changed afterwards, and grades the forecasts of the games that are over.

Do not edit the files by hand. The job reads back what it wrote. It refuses to continue from a state file it cannot check, to change a history line or a result that is already there, to add to results files it cannot check, and to write the forecasts of a day a second time.

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `v1/slate.json` | The board: the upcoming games as of the latest snapshot, each with its line in that snapshot, its opening line, Elo's chance and, for a game of the day, the frozen forecast of the points-and-rest model. With them the wins and losses so far of the sportsbooks' favorite and of each model's, and the results of the last eight days. Replaced by every snapshot. |
| `v1/state.json` | What the job remembers between runs: the last slot it recorded, the API credits left, the first and the latest line of each game, and what the daily work last noted, which includes Elo's ratings and the forecasts of the day. A game stays until 14 days after its start. |
| `v1/history/YYYY-MM-DD.ndjson` | One line per game per snapshot, in one file per UTC date. Lines are only ever added. |
| `v1/results/YYYY-MM.ndjson` | One line per game that is over, in one file per UTC month of the games' starts: the final score, the game's last line from before its start and the verdict on that line, and what each model said on the morning of the game with the verdict on that. Lines are only ever added, and a game is recorded once. |
| `v1/predictions/YYYY-MM-DD.json` | The forecasts for the games of one day, written once, on the morning of that day, and never changed: for each game Elo's chance with the two ratings it comes from, the points-and-rest model's chance and expected margin with the three parts of the margin, and the sportsbooks' line as the job had it then. |
| `v1/model.json` | Where the two models stand: every team's Elo rating and its rating a week earlier, its points-and-rest rating and how well that rating is known, its wins and losses, whether both models could be built from the results, and which parameter files and which commit of the code the numbers come from. Rebuilt once a day. |
| `v1/record.json` | What the results add up to, for the sportsbooks' favorite and for each model's: the wins and losses, the accuracy with a 95% interval, the Brier score and the log loss, the results by band of the favorite's probability and by day, and the three biggest upsets. Also what the home team every time would have won, and for each model the games in which it and the sportsbooks picked different winners and its Brier score next to theirs. Rebuilt from all result lines once a day. |
| `v1-dryrun/` | The files of the snapshots and the results for preseason games, written until 17 October 2026 to rehearse the job on real games. It is not part of the record, and the models, which are for the games of the season, are not run on it. |
| `nba-predictions-app/vercel.json` | Not data. Vercel builds the `nba-predictions-app` folder of every branch that is pushed to this repository, and this file tells it not to deploy this one. |

The fields of each file, the grading rules, the schedule and the rules the job follows are described in [`pipeline/README.md` on `main`](https://github.com/shubhroses/nba-game-prediction/blob/main/pipeline/README.md), and the two models in [`pipeline/model/README.md`](https://github.com/shubhroses/nba-game-prediction/blob/main/pipeline/model/README.md). `schema` is 1 in the JSON files and stays 1 when a field is added, so a reader has to ignore the fields it does not know.

Of the odds, the files hold derived figures only: for each game the median, the lowest and the highest of the sportsbooks' home win probabilities with each sportsbook's margin removed, the number of sportsbooks, and their names when there are two or more that do not all give the same probability. The responses of the odds provider and the prices in them are not published. Of the scores, the files hold the final score of each game that is over.

The forecasts are worked out from those final scores and the schedule, and from nothing else. The Elo ratings start from the NBA Elo ratings that FiveThirtyEight published under the [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), as they stood in June 2023.
